sentences.text: Reports described that the SARS outbreak of 2003 was often marked by a degree of disorder and confusion, with healthcare providers on the front-lines facing a huge lack of basic information about the nature of SARS, especially at the outset.

Doctors, health workers, hospital management, and public health officials did not have the benefit of knowing all that was known post-SARS, and those at Scarborough Grace Hospital were literally learning about the disease as every day of the outbreak passed and were having to make decisions based on little knowledge and without a full understanding of the severity of the situation.

By April 7, 2003, there had been no known transmission at Grace Hospital since detailed infection control procedures had been put in place, and by April 8, 2003, many hospitals were off Code Orange status and surgeries had resumed.

Public health officials in York and Toronto traced and quarantine contacts with good results, and the outbreak management teams and leaders of the local public health units were identified as those who deserve greatest credit for containing the SARS outbreak.
Ten people had died from SARS in Canada.
The report was dedicated to those who died from SARS, those who suffered from it, those who fought the disease, and all those affected by it.
